findings.calibration: P2 race: behavior depends on read/write interleaving; the existing worker has an uncaught settings read in evaluate, so a valid first update can terminate the forecast owner. The deterministic rejected-first-CAS variant also blocks later default reads.
findings.evidence_kind: Static source counterexample; not executed by this read-only reviewer.
findings.recommendation: For the deterministic absent-store conflict, reject expected_revision != 0 before mkdir/os.open when the store is absent, retaining the transaction-protected reread for competing creates. Also ensure first initialization is published atomically to readers, or use narrowly verified in-progress initialization handling that never turns an incompatible/corrupt existing database into defaults. Do not reset a database or weaken immutable history or CAS.
regression_sketches: With a fresh TemporaryDirectory home, assert set_seconds(home,SOL/USD,17,1) raises revision_conflict; then assert no preferences file exists, settings equals default 10/revision 0 and a subsequent set(...,0) succeeds.

Pause a valid first writer between file creation and initialization commit; query settings concurrently and assert a complete default or complete committed setting, never incompatible; assert the worker remains running. Keep this deterministic with synchronization rather than real sleeps.

scenarios.impact: A subsequent settings(home,SOL/USD) sees an existing empty file and raises forecast_preferences_incompatible instead of returning the untouched default 10/revision 0. A rejected update changes future behavior until a valid revision-0 write repairs initialization.
scenarios.trace: os.open creates the file. BEGIN IMMEDIATE initializes settings, application_id and triggers. The revision comparison raises a conflict because no row exists. The connection context rolls initialization back, but the external file creation survives.
scenarios.trigger: Absent forecast-preferences.sqlite3; call set_seconds(home, SOL/USD, 17, expected_revision=1).

scenarios.impact: settings raises forecast_preferences_incompatible. forecast.py:298 calls it without a guard; forecast.py:641-643 has no loop catch, so this read can terminate the display owner. It can also fail a local report read.
scenarios.trace: Schedule the read after os.open/close and before schema/application_id commit. Readonly SQLite sees the empty/uncommitted store with application_id 0.
scenarios.trigger: Absent store; a valid first set_seconds(...,expected_revision=0) overlaps settings().
